question.problem:
If $P$ is a statement, $\text{t}$ is a tautology, and $\text{c}$ is a contradiction, complete the following table of logical equivalences.

| Statement | Is Logically Equivalent To |
| --- | --- |
| $\text{c}∧\text{c}$ | {{field-1}} |
| $\text{c}∨\text{t}$ | {{field-2}} |
| $P∧\text{c}$ | {{field-3}} |
| $\text{c}∨¬P$ | {{field-4}} |

current_example.problem:
If $P$ is a statement, $\textbf t$ is a tautology, and $\textbf c$ is a contradiction, complete the following table of logical equivalences.

| Statement | Is Logically Equivalent To |
| --- | --- |
| $\textbf t \land \textbf c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\phantom{\color{blue}P}}$ |
| $\textbf t \lor \textbf c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\phantom{\color{blue}P}}$ |
| $P \land \textbf c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\phantom{\color{blue}P}}$ |
| $P \lor \textbf c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\phantom{\color{blue}P}}$ |
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall the following properties of tautologies and contradictions:

$$
\begin{aligned}A∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & A∧\text{t} & =A \\ A∨\text{c}=A\, &  & A∧\text{c} & =\text{c} \\ \text{t}∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{t}∧\text{t} & =\text{t} \\ \text{t}∨\text{c}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{t}∧\text{c} & =\text{c} \\ \text{c}∨\text{t}=\text{t}\, &  & \text{c}∧\text{t} & =\text{c} \\ \text{c}∨\text{c}=\text{c}\, &  & \text{c}∧\text{c} & =\text{c}\end{aligned}
$$

The completed table is shown below.

| Statement | Is Logically Equivalent To |
| --- | --- |
| $\textbf t \land \textbf  c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textbf c}$ |
| $\textbf t \lor \textbf  c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textbf t}$ |
| $P \land \textbf c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\textbf c}$ |
| $P \lor \textbf c$ | $\bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}P}$ |
